anchor.snippet: static void *load_proc(void *user, const char *name) { (void)user; return SDL_GL_GetProcAddress(name); }

entries.note:
Both of the pack's layers take their entry points from whoever opens them — `re_gpu_open` takes a `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, `re_seam_open` takes a `get_proc` — so the pack links no windowing library and no GL library, and a consumer that loads GL some other way (a headset runtime, a different window toolkit) passes its own loader here and changes nothing else.

That is the same property spec 122 established for the device layer, and it is why this file is the only one in the seam-backed renderer that mentions SDL.

`re_seam_target_adopt` exists because of this call. The seam's frame takes a target rather than assuming the default framebuffer — a decision the render-to-texture test forced (spec 124's 'the frame takes its target' section) — and on OpenGL the window's back buffer already IS a target, name 0. Adopting it keeps one code path in `backend_seam.c` for both the window and an offscreen image.

`seam_host_vk.c` and `seam_host_metal.m` acquire a swapchain image here instead, which is the whole reason acquire is a host call and not something the backend does. The trailing 0 is the format argument adopt grew for them: OpenGL needs none, because a framebuffer name carries its own attachments, and Vulkan cannot recover one from a VkImageView at all.

anchor.snippet: /* glReadPixels hands back bottom-up and SDL wants top-down, which is the one orientation

entries.note:
The seam's own targets agree on orientation across all three APIs — row 0 means the same thing everywhere, which is what let `backend_seam.c` carry one Y formula and one scissor expression. `glReadPixels` does not: it is specified bottom-up regardless.

So the flip belongs to the OpenGL host, not to the seam and not to the backend. A Vulkan or Metal host reading back its own image will not need one, and pushing this into shared code would give them a flip they would have to undo. The committed reference frames are the thing that would catch it either way — a whole-image vertical flip is not subtle — which is why it can be stated once here rather than defended by its own test.

`GL_PACK_ALIGNMENT`, `GL_RGBA` and `GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE` are written as their values because this file includes no GL header — it reaches GL only through `SDL_GL_GetProcAddress`, the same way the seam does, so there is nothing to include on a platform where the header ships a 1.1 subset.

The alignment call matters: the default pack alignment is 4, and a snapshot of a window whose width is not a multiple of 4 would be read back with per-row padding and come out sheared. It is guarded rather than required because a driver missing `glPixelStorei` is still worth a snapshot at the default alignment.
